messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple GitHub Actions runners failing across org repos (429/502). Failed deploy jobs detected. Affected workflows: redwood/*-deploy, redwood/hotfix-* (root ts: 1862400000)

jamie (oncall): seeing the same. CI dashboard shows repeated 429s from api.github.com during artifact upload. Can someone confirm if this is a GitHub-side outage or our runner config?

katie (release): deploy-bot reports: `job redwood/hotfix-2026.03/build -> failed: upload artifact (status 502)`. We have a critical hotfix that needs to go out (auth token rotation). Builds are blocked.

deploy-bot: Failed pipeline summary: 12 failed workflows in last 10m, earliest failure 1862400005. Steps failing: upload-artifact, publish-to-packages. Error snippets: `POST https://api.github.com/repos/redwood/packages/uploads -> 502 Bad Gateway`

jamie (oncall): ok triage plan: (1) confirm GitHub status, (2) attempt manual reruns / alternate runner, (3) look for cached artifacts or internal mirror, (4) if builds blocked and customer-impacting, mitigate via feature-flag rollback or config toggle.

cheng (sre): I pulled github status: https://www.githubstatus.com/ shows degraded performance for "Actions API" and "Packages" starting ~1862399980. Also seeing spikes in rate limit 429 on our side.

katie (release): confirmed. Trying to rerun on our self-hosted runners: `./scripts/ci/rerun.sh redwood/hotfix-2026.03 --runner self-hosted-us-west` -> initial runs are failing on the package publish step (503). The build completes but publish to GitHub Packages fails.

jamie (oncall): Can we publish to an alternate registry (internal Artifactory / S3) as a temporary path? Need to get the hotfix out.

cheng (sre): We have cached container images/artifacts in S3 for a previous CI run. If katie can rebuild and push image directly to our registry (internal ECR) without using GitHub Packages, that might bypass the outage. Steps: build locally on a runner, tag with internal ECR URI, push.

katie (release): trying manual build on a self-hosted runner now. Build logs: `yarn build -> success`, `docker build -> success`, `docker push internal.ecr.redwood-inference.com/hotfix:2026.03.15 -> succeeded` :thumbsup: but subsequent deploy pipeline that pulls artifact from GitHub Packages still fails. I updated the deploy manifest to point to internal ECR image for this hotfix. Pushing change via a direct git commit to main? can't because github api pushes are flakey. I can push from the runner directly via git over SSH to allow branch update.

elaine (cs): Heads up — CS is seeing a support ticket from AcmeCorp reporting login errors in their production cluster. They said the fix was supposed to be deployed this morning. If we miss the window, they'll escalate.

jamie (oncall): severity: P1 for deploy-blocker impacting customer hotfix. Paging on-call SRE and release. @cheng you own mitigation of CI block, @katie you own packaging bypass, @elaine please collect customer impact details. I'll open an incident in the tracker.

monitoring-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-030 (P1) due to third-party GitHub Actions/Packages outage affecting deploy pipelines. Link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2026-030

cheng (sre): escalated to GH support via status page ticket (ticket #123456). Also opened support case via our TAM. Quoting: "Multiple 502/429 when uploading artifacts and publishing packages from our runners, affecting critical deploys."

katie (release): manual push via SSH to the deploy server worked; we've staged the hotfix image and started a canary deploy to 3 hosts using the internal ECR image. Canary logs look good so far: auth token rotation applied, no errors in logs.

jamie (oncall): good. Can we do a controlled rollout to prod without touching GitHub workflows? Keep rollback plan ready.

katie (release): yes, using our deploy tooling directly: `rwd-deploy --image internal.ecr.redwood-inference.com/hotfix:2026.03.15 --env prod --subset canary=3`

deploy-bot: Manual deploy initiated by katie (release). Status: canary 3/3 started at 1862400360. Watch logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/canary/hotfix-2026.03.15

elaine (cs): I updated AcmeCorp with interim ETA: 30m, gave public workaround (clear cache but this is not reliable). They replied asking for a rollback option if not fixed.

jamie (oncall): if GitHub outage persists, we should update runbook: allow direct image pushes to internal registry for hotfixes and run manual deploy steps. Note: needs an audit entry for bypass.

cheng (sre): added temporary ACL entry to allow runners to push directly to ECR from self-hosted jobs. Also validated credential rotation.

katie (release): pushed notes to #release-notes and created a short runbook snippet in the incident page with commands we used. Snippet: ```
# manual build + push
yarn install && yarn build
docker build -t internal.ecr.redwood-inference.com/hotfix:2026.03.15 .
aws ecr get-login-password | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin internal.ecr.redwood-inference.com
docker push internal.ecr.redwood-inference.com/hotfix:2026.03.15
# deploy
rwd-deploy --image internal.ecr.redwood-inference.com/hotfix:2026.03.15 --env prod --subset canary=3
```

jamie (oncall): good capture. @cheng please keep GH support ticket updated. Also document any credential/ACL changes for security review.

cheng (sre): GH support replied: "We're investigating an issue with Actions API and Packages; no ETA yet." They asked for failure logs and request IDs. I uploaded logs and our request IDs.

monitoring-bot: Performance metric: failed_action_api_calls increased 4x at 1862399990; package_registry_502_count = 78 in last 15m.

elaine (cs): AcmeCorp acknowledges our canary deploy. They requested that we coordinate a follow-up call after full rollout. I scheduled a 30m bridge at +1h.

jamie (oncall): handoff: I'm heading offline for a brief break at 1862400440. @cheng you'll take primary until I return (or until SEC fires). Summary for handoff: GitHub Actions/Packages degraded, manual ECR bypass used to deploy hotfix canary (3 hosts). CS notified. Severity P1. CHANGES: temporary ACL for ECR pushes. Keep GH ticket open.

cheng (sre): acknowledged. I'll monitor canary, escalate if errors. I'll keep the incident page updated and coordinate with katie for full rollout.

katie (release): canary 3/3 healthy at 1862400580; rolling to remaining hosts now. ETA full rollout 20m.

deploy-bot: Deployment progress: 3/3 canary healthy, rolling to 25% of prod hosts. No errors reported so far.

jamie (oncall): thanks team. If GH status becomes healthy, we'll switch back to normal workflows and publish packages from CI and re-enable automated artifact uploads. Until then, keep using internal ECR for emergency patches.

cheng (sre): noted. I'll also add a post-incident action item: evaluate CI artifact mirrors and a fallback to our artifact proxy to avoid single-vendor blocking.

elaine (cs): customer call set. I'll take notes and follow up if AcmeCorp requests SLA credits.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigation in progress. Next update scheduled at 1862400900 or on important events.

katie (release): full rollout completed at 1862400740. Monitoring looks clean. Marking hotfix as deployed. :tada:

cheng (sre): closing the fire for now but keeping incident open until GitHub confirms resolution and we restore normal publish pipeline. Postmortem owner: cheng. Action items: CI mirror plan, update runbooks, audit ACL change.

jamie (oncall): thanks all. Passing to cheng for follow-up. Going to rest. :wave:
